steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Online and social media encompass websites, social networking platforms, blogs, vlogs, wikis, and apps — media products that exist on the internet and often enable audience participation.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Websites use conventions: homepage, navigation menu, banner, content sections, hyperlinks, multimedia (images, video, audio), and calls to action.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Social media platforms (Instagram, TikTok, X/Twitter, YouTube, Snapchat) enable user-generated content, social networking, and algorithmic content distribution.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Prosumer culture: audiences are no longer just consumers — they produce, share, and remix content. This democratises media but also creates challenges with misinformation and quality.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What is the 'prosumer' and how has digital media created this role? | Q: How do algorithms affect what audiences see on social media? | Q: Evaluate the impact of social media on democratic participation.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always name specific platforms (TikTok, Instagram, YouTube) and their conventions Discuss algorithms and their impact on audiences and content Consider both the democratising potential and the risks of online media
